From: Elliot Shaw <elliot@nimbuslabs.ai>

Date: Thu, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cohort conversion credits — trigger & fallback options

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — our cohort teams were impressed with the latency numbers and the prefix caching explanation. Quick follow-up on the promotional credits side:

We received a 60k token cohort credit from our accelerator partner that we'd like to apply toward an initial Dedicated pilot. Our concern is upfront conversion: if we move to Dedicated and spike (we expect a burst during demo week), can Redwood provide a fallback to hosted burst capacity or automatically switch back to cohort credits so we're not stuck paying for unused reserved GPU hours?

Specific asks:
- Can credits be used to cover an initial Dedicated reservation (even if reserved capacity is partially unused)?
- Is there a built-in trigger we can set (e.g., 75% consumption) that converts remaining credits into a short-term hosted fallback for spikes?
- What would a one-time promotional exception look like (e.g., pro-rated top-up / buffer)?

I've attached a short demo summary and our expected usage profile for the next 90 days (nimbus-demo-summary.pdf). Marta from our program team is CC'd — she handles billing during the cohort.

Appreciate any guidance — aiming to finalize before next Monday so we can schedule the Dedicated pool.

— Elliot
Elliot Shaw
Head of Platform Partnerships
Nimbus Labs
elliot@nimbuslabs.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Hi Elliot — thanks for the clear note and for sharing the demo summary. Looping Vanessa for commercial visibility (she owns cohort promotions).

Short answers up front:
- Yes: we can apply cohort/promotional credits toward a Dedicated pilot, but we usually gate by a conversion policy to protect capacity economics.
- We can implement a consumption trigger (we typically use 70–80%) to move to a fallback path. That fallback can be either: 1) automatic routing to hosted burst (pay-as-you-go) for token spikes, or 2) a short-term pro-rated Dedicated top-up paid via card/invoice.
- For a one-time exception, we can offer a small grace buffer (30k tokens) on top of the 60k cohort credit for the first 30 days to cover demo-week volatility, then enforce the trigger. Any remaining promotional balance after conversion is handled per the addendum.

Proposed next steps:
1) If you confirm the 90-day usage estimates in the attachment, I'll draft a promo-addendum with: the 30k buffer, a 75% conversion trigger, and a pro-rated top-up pricing table for overflow.
2) Vanessa and I will review the commercial margins and confirm approval window (we typically need internal signoff within 48 hours for exceptions).
3) If accepted, we'll send a DocuSign addendum and schedule a 30-minute kickoff to pin the Dedicated pool sizing.

If that direction works, please confirm and we'll move to docs.

Best,

--
Priyom Das

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 5 May 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Cohort conversion credits — approval needed for promo exception

Vanessa / Ben — forwarding Nimbus thread and demo summary. They want to convert 60k cohort tokens into an initial Dedicated pilot but need protection for demo-week spikes. I proposed a 30k-token grace buffer + a 75% consumption trigger that flips overflow to hosted burst or a pro-rated top-up.

Why I think this is reasonable:
- Cohort programs are high-visibility leads; small short-term buffer helps conversion to paid Dedicated.
- We can protect capacity economics by using a high trigger (75%) and capping the buffer at 30k for 30 days.
- We should require a billing contact (Marta) and a card on file for any pro-rated top-ups beyond the buffer.

Proposed commercial terms for internal approval (short):
- Free buffer: 30,000 tokens applied immediately to the Dedicated reservation for 30 days.
- Trigger: when total Dedicated consumption reaches 75% of the reserved tranche, remaining promo balance pauses and overflow routes to hosted burst at standard pay-as-you-go rates (or a one-time pro-rated Dedicated top-up if Nimbus prefers).
- Visibility: cost & token burn reporting to be shared daily during the 30-day window.
- Expiration: any unused promo tokens at 30 days are returned to accelerator pool (no cash value).

Attachments: promo-addendum.docx (draft terms) and the original demo summary.

Can you both confirm: 1) margin OK for a 30k buffer? 2) Any legal/compliance flags? If Ben is good on pricing, Vanessa — please greenlight the exception and I'll send to Nimbus for signature.

Thanks,
Priyom
